key_concepts: Xylem transports water and dissolved nutrients upward from roots
Phloem transports sugars and other organic nutrients downward from leaves
Transpiration is water loss through leaf pores after absorption by roots
Root pressure pushes sap upward in xylem due to osmotic pressure in roots
Capillary action moves liquid through narrow spaces without external force
Sieve tubes are phloem cells that transport food materials
Vascular bundles contain xylem and phloem for transport
Translocation moves soluble food from one plant part to another
Guard cells regulate stomatal opening and gas exchange
Stomata are tiny pores that allow gas exchange
Root hairs absorb water and nutrients from soil
Xylem vessels are made of dead cells
